children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! An 8-year-old is within the eligible age range for Child Benefit.

Now, could you tell me whether you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you, or does he live with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, I have a couple of follow-up questions.

Do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep (for example, by paying for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing to his accommodation)? If so, how much do you contribute and how often?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes and other bits and pieces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that. To determine your eligibility, I need to understand the amount you contribute.

The Child Benefit rate is currently around £25.60 per week for a first child. To qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you would need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them.

Could you tell me roughly how much you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week (or the monthly equivalent)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I give about £10 a week towards his things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

Since you're contributing around £10 per week, this is less than the Child Benefit rate (approximately £25.60 per week for the first child). To qualify for Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else, you would typically need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment.

I have one more question: Is Alex's mum already claiming Child Benefit for him, or do you know if anyone else is claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's why:

1. **Alex lives with someone else**: Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, you would need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (approximately £25.60 per week) towards his upkeep to qualify. Your contribution of around £10 per week, while helpful, is below this threshold.

2. **Only one person can claim**: Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him and he lives with her, she has the primary entitlement to the benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future — for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you increase your contributions to at least the Child Benefit rate — you may want to revisit your eligibility.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
